solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cockney worker accepting dull job fast

indicators.note: a word that accepts another takes it in, so the worker's letters hold the job's letters

parts.note: a worker is a hand; Cockneys drop the H, giving 'AND
a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: A London labourer takes on boring work quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the initial H of a word, and a worker is a hand. 'Fast' is not speed here but firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held fast is firmly secured, as a boat moored in place is.

clue.text: Player given hand, being latest in series to receive gold

indicators.note: a word receiving another takes it inside, so the series letters wrap round the gold

parts.note: nth means the latest or umpteenth in a series
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A sportsperson, dealt a role as the newest in a run, wins gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, each dealt a hand; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge each of four seats, named after compass points, is a player who is dealt cards.

clue.text: Old barbarian — cause of complaint — leading demo

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders of old
a germ causes an illness, or complaint
arch means chief or leading, as in arch-villain

explanation.surface: An ancient barbarian with a grievance heads a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' means an illness, not a grievance. A hunger march was a 1930s protest walk by the unemployed, like the Jarrow March in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a protest, and this was a long-distance protest walk by jobless workers.

clue.text: Sort of mirror on small badge cut off

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: cutting off a word loses its end, so the last letter of the badge goes

parts.note: an emblem is a badge

explanation.surface: A kind of mirror is mounted on a small badge that has been trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be like something is a sort of mirroring of it, copying its look.

clue.text: Tremble when passing notes around, short ones

parts.note: demise is a death, or passing

indicators.note: the notes sit around the tremble, its letters inside theirs

parts.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale, so two or more are mis
to quaver is to tremble

explanation.surface: Someone shakes while handing round brief written messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing notes' looks like handing over messages; 'passing' is death and 'notes' are musical. 'Short ones' points back to notes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are among the briefest musical notes, each a thirty-second of a whole note.

clue.text: With this music, see the joint jumping?

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
to hop is to jump on one foot

explanation.surface: This music gets the whole place hopping, a hip joint in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' also suggests a club, making the jumping venue part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: This genre is the rap and breakdance music born in the Bronx in the 1970s.

clue.text: Big cheese sandwich on cholesterol-packed wraps

indicators.note: the phrase wraps round the answer, holding its letters inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A grand cheese sandwich bulging with fat is served in tortilla wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites 'wraps' as food; it is the containment signal, the answer spanning sandwicH ON CHOlesterol.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is an important boss, and this is American slang for the person in charge.

clue.text: Drop litter and stuff

definitions.meaning: for a sow, to give birth to a litter of young
to stuff oneself is to eat greedily, to gorge

explanation.surface: Someone tosses rubbish around and other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop litter' reads as fly-tipping; here it is a sow giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are verbs: a sow farrowing its young, and gorging on food greedily.

clue.text: American monk with a halo that's slipping

indicators.note: a slipping halo has its letters slide out of order, so the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US citizen who is a monk with a halo going askew.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a native of one US state, so an American in the narrower sense.

clue.text: For all to see, what FDR did for the world

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing, fit for all to see
President Franklin D Roosevelt ran the US

explanation.surface: A tribute to what President Roosevelt achieved for the world, on public display.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating meaning anyone may watch. 'The world' is not Earth but a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet may be called a world, and this one is the seventh from the Sun.

clue.text: Game ending in hullabaloo, filming abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A movie shoot was called off after the uproar at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending in' takes the final O of hullabaloo; 'abandoned' shuffles it with FILMING.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a scaled-down putting game played round obstacles, often at seaside resorts.

clue.text: What's said to drive away mule?

indicators.note: the clue asks for something spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: shoo is the word called out to drive an animal off

explanation.surface: What do you call out to send a stubborn mule packing?
explanation.walkthrough: The mule is not the animal but a backless slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: A mule is a backless slip-on piece of footwear, so a kind of slipper.

clue.text: Wrongly believed hotel is obliged to put on film

indicators.note: the hotel and obligation pieces are placed on, after, the film

parts.note: a mist is a thin film, as on glass
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ought means is obliged to

explanation.surface: A hotel had to screen a movie, someone mistakenly thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' is a thin layer, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic past tense meaning held a mistaken opinion.

clue.text: The responsibility of school to carry out: head of history fired

parts.note: something up to you is your responsibility
a high is a high school
to do is to carry out

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: It falls to the school to act once the head of history is sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like sacked; here it means worked up. The phrase is Scottish for highly agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fired up, excited or agitated, matches this Scottish idiom for a state of high anxiety.

clue.text: Swindle flourished: moneylenders flee

parts.note: fl. abbreviates floruit, Latin for flourished, used of dates
the IMF, International Monetary Fund, lends money to nations
to lam is slang for to run off

explanation.surface: A con thrived and the loan sharks ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: FL is the abbreviation for floruit, used where only someone's active years are known.
explanation.definitionFit: This is nonsense or trickery used to cheat someone, a con.

clue.text: Erotic performer's comeback reportedly overlooked by Hollywood police?

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: in a down entry a piece overlooked by another sits beneath it

parts.note: the LAPD is the Los Angeles Police Department, which covers Hollywood

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a comeback is a retort or answer

explanation.surface: A stripper's return to the stage, it is said, escaped the notice of LA police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comeback' looks like a return; it is a retort. ANCER sounds like the second part.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dancer who performs erotically close to, or on, a seated customer.

clue.text: Volume's dedication to its author?

definitions.meaning: a volume is a large book; the 's is short for is
a book dedicated to its own writer would say these two words

explanation.surface: A book is inscribed to the person who wrote it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word into two, the dedication of a vain writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A volume is a big heavy book, and a vain dedication would read as two words meaning for myself.

clue.text: What old sailors must follow to go beyond headland

definitions.text: What old sailors must follow to go beyond headland

parts.words: What old sailors must follow to go beyond headland
parts.note: sailing ships going between oceans had to round the southernmost tip of South America; and the word for a headland comes before the second part

explanation.walkthrough: Old sailing ships passed this South American point to get from the Atlantic to the Pacific; HORN also follows CAPE (headland) in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the southernmost headland of South America, rounded by sailing ships changing oceans.

clue.text: Turn down short side road

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to spurn is to turn down or reject

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn into a brief side road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn down' looks like a driving direction; it means reject.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch road leaving a main route is called this, as in a motorway branch.

clue.text: As Di having left, lively party's ending

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: the name having left means its letters go from the party word

parts.note: a shindig is a lively party
taken as written

explanation.surface: With Princess Di gone, the spirited party is winding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ending' looks like the close of the party; it is the definition, a verb form meaning putting a stop to.
explanation.definitionFit: Quashing a ruling or protest is putting a stop to it, ending it.

clue.text: Hanging underneath leg, sway

indicators.note: in a down entry the sway piece goes underneath the leg piece

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
hold means power or influence, sway

explanation.surface: Dangling below a leg and swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side in cricket, the half of the field behind the batter's legs, is also called on.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter left hanging is suspended, waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: A commotion's beginning in church — natural to laugh

indicators.note: the A and the first letter go inside the church abbreviation
a word's beginning is its first letter

parts.note: innate means natural, inborn

explanation.surface: A row breaks out in church, and laughing comes naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare verb means to laugh loudly and immoderately, to guffaw.

clue.text: French writer rejected fancy English

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to dig is slang for to like or fancy

explanation.surface: A French author turned down showy English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to like. The writer is André, the Nobel-winning novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: André, author of The Immoralist, was a French novelist and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Last of liquid? Tip it down sink

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: tipping it down is British slang for pouring with rain

explanation.surface: The dregs of a drink: pour them down the sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip it down' looks like pouring; it is a British phrase for heavy rain. 'Sink' is a verb, to swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink a drink is to down it completely, emptying the glass.

clue.text: Gas that is to escape slowly after houseroom evacuated

indicators.note: the slow escape comes after the emptied houseroom

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is

indicators.note: an evacuated word is emptied of its inside, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: to ooze is to seep out slowly

explanation.surface: Leaking gas seeps from an emptied room of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is not fuel but idle talk. 'Evacuated' empties HOUSEROOM to its ends, H and M.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chatter, and this means to chat sociably, often to ingratiate.

clue.text: One's not moved border up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hem is the border of a cloth

explanation.surface: Someone stays put when the frontier moves upward.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the sound an unimpressed person makes: an expression of indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection expresses indifference, the reaction of someone left unimpressed.

clue.text: Unconventional lad, tho' far from fashionable

indicators.note: unconventional means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A quirky lad, though anything but trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hackneyed and long past its time is out of date, the opposite of trendy.

clue.text: Men rebuked for bloomer

parts.note: OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
chid is an old past tense of chide, to rebuke

explanation.surface: Soldiers told off for a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and this is a showy tropical flowering plant.

clue.text: Light oriental dish around noon, one without starter

indicators.note: the dish goes around the noon letter

parts.note: sushi is a Japanese dish

indicators.note: a word without its starter loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A light Asian meal around midday, eaten without a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the meal; it is the noun, daylight.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the sun is the plain meaning, daylight warming the scene.
